questions.topic: WW1 Poetry — conventions, devices, form and critical commentary
questions.prompt: POETRY WRITING PRACTICE — Write 10–14 lines on conflict using at least three purposeful devices or structural choices. Then add a 3-sentence critical commentary explaining your choices.

markPoints: clear perspective on conflict
at least three purposeful poetic or structural choices
control of imagery or sound rather than random device-listing
a meaningful structural development or turn
critical commentary explaining how choices create meaning
answer.modelAnswer: A successful response should make a deliberate choice about voice and perspective, use imagery and structure consistently, and then explain why those choices were made. The commentary should identify specific decisions—for example a repeated image, caesura, enjambment or a turn in tone—and link them to the poem's meaning.

note.title: WW1 Poetry — conventions, devices, form and critical commentary
note.overview: Analyse poetic form and devices precisely, then apply them deliberately in original conflict writing and commentary.
learningGoals: Analyse how a device contributes to a larger idea.
Comment on form and structural development.
Explain creative choices in a critical commentary.
mustMemoriseRules: Device labels do not have fixed effects; context matters.
Form is meaningful when you explain how its pattern or disruption shapes reading.
A critical commentary explains choices, not just what the poem is about.
workedExamples: A traditional form can create productive tension with disturbing subject matter.
A volta can reframe an earlier image and force the reader to reconsider the poem’s argument.
commonMistakes: Assuming all WW1 poetry presents the same viewpoint.
Writing commentary that simply paraphrases the poem.
detailedExplanation: The curriculum scope and assessed skills are verified against the official Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 English Curriculum Outline 2026-27.
Practice articles, extracts and poem-like lines in this bank are newly written for the app and are not copies of the school’s assessment materials.
Long article, poem and presentation responses are practice/self-check tasks and do not by themselves create formal Mastery evidence.
examTips: Explain how structure changes emphasis or audience response.
Use terminology accurately but keep the interpretation central.
Compare writers through ideas and methods, not two separate mini-essays.
quickCheck: Analyse how a device contributes to a larger idea.
Comment on form and structural development.
Explain creative choices in a critical commentary.
beforeStartingPractice: Recall the core methods and command words before beginning.
